aluminum.name: Aluminum Alloys

shallow.note: Continuous drilling OK. Use high RPM, flood coolant.

medium.note: Chip break every 2×D if chips wrap around drill.

veryDeep.note: Full retract peck every 1×D. Consider parabolic drill.

aluminum.coolantNote: Flood coolant essential. Air blast can cause chip welding.
specialTips: Use sharp, polished flute drills to prevent chip sticking
ZrN or DLC coating reduces built-up edge
Increase RPM before reducing peck depth

mild_steel.name: Mild Steel (1018, A36)

shallow.note: Continuous drilling OK with proper feeds.

medium.note: Chip break every 1.5×D prevents chip nesting.

veryDeep.note: Full retract peck every 0.75×D. Use coolant-through drill.

mild_steel.coolantNote: Flood coolant required. Through-spindle coolant for deep holes.
specialTips: Stringy chips indicate feed too light - increase IPR
TiN or TiCN coating improves chip breaking
Parabolic flutes excel in deep holes

alloy_steel.name: Alloy Steel (4140, 4340)

shallow.note: Chip break helps with heat dissipation.

medium.note: Peck every 1×D essential for tool life.

deep.note: Peck every 0.75×D. Reduce speed 10-15% for deep holes.

veryDeep.note: Full retract peck every 0.5×D. Coolant-through REQUIRED.

alloy_steel.coolantNote: High-pressure flood coolant required. EP additives recommended.
specialTips: Cobalt or carbide drills strongly recommended
TiAlN coating critical for heat resistance
Dwell at bottom causes work hardening - avoid

stainless_304.name: Stainless Steel (304, 316)

shallow.note: Chip break recommended even for shallow holes.

medium.note: Peck every 0.75×D. NEVER dwell - causes work hardening.

veryDeep.note: Peck every 0.3×D with full retract. Coolant-through drill REQUIRED.

stainless_304.coolantNote: HIGH-PRESSURE flood coolant CRITICAL. Minimum 300 PSI through-spindle for deep holes.
specialTips: ⚠️ NEVER let drill dwell or stop in cut - causes instant work hardening
Keep drill cutting at all times - constant feed pressure
Cobalt M42 or carbide drills REQUIRED
AlTiN or TiAlN coating essential for heat resistance
Reduce speed 20-30% compared to mild steel

stainless_17_4.name: Stainless Steel (17-4 PH, 15-5)

shallow.note: Peck every 0.75×D even for shallow holes.

medium.note: Peck every 0.5×D. Maintain constant cutting action.

deep.note: Peck every 0.35×D. This is pushing limits - use premium tooling.

veryDeep.note: Consider EDM or gun drilling. If drilling: 0.25×D peck, fresh sharp drill.

stainless_17_4.coolantNote: HIGH-PRESSURE flood coolant MANDATORY. 500+ PSI through-spindle recommended.
specialTips: ⚠️ Premium carbide drill REQUIRED - HSS will fail quickly
Plan for multiple drill changes on production runs
Work hardened layer forms instantly if drill dwells
Consider spot drilling with carbide spot drill first
Through-spindle coolant is nearly mandatory

titanium.name: Titanium (6Al-4V)
titanium.tendency: Low thermal conductivity, galling, fire risk

shallow.note: Peck every 0.5×D. Heat concentrates at drill point.

medium.note: Peck every 0.35×D with partial retract for cooling.

deep.note: Full retract peck every 0.25×D. Allow coolant to flood hole.

veryDeep.note: Extreme caution. 0.2×D peck. Consider alternative methods (EDM, trepanning).

titanium.coolantNote: HIGH-VOLUME, HIGH-PRESSURE flood coolant CRITICAL. Fire extinguisher nearby for chip fires.
specialTips: 🔥 FIRE RISK: Titanium chips can spontaneously ignite
Keep chip pile wet with coolant at all times
Have Class D fire extinguisher readily available
Premium carbide with AlCrN coating recommended
Very low speed (50-100 SFM) essential
Sharp tools only - replace at first sign of wear

inconel.name: Inconel/Hastelloy (718, 625)
inconel.tendency: Extreme work hardening, heat concentration, rapid tool wear

shallow.note: Peck every 0.35×D even for very shallow holes.

deep.note: Peck every 0.2×D. Multiple tool changes expected.

veryDeep.note: STRONGLY consider EDM. If drilling: 0.15×D peck, expect frequent tool changes.

inconel.coolantNote: MAXIMUM PRESSURE flood coolant MANDATORY. Through-spindle coolant essential.
specialTips: ⚠️ Most difficult common material to drill
Premium nano-grain carbide with nACo or AlTiN coating
Tool life measured in inches, not holes
Budget for multiple drill changes per hole
Work hardened layer 0.003-0.005" deep forms instantly
Consider EDM for deep holes or production quantities

deep.note: Peck for chip clearing, not chip breaking.
